text: {"status":"STABLE","core_findings":["Sampled training separation is strong across all four categories: pairwise accuracy ranges from 92.92% in Electronics to 99.65% in CDs_and_Vinyl, measured over 10,374–15,341 valid positions per category from ten batches. These position-weighted observations do not establish held-out ranking quality; validation measurements and uncertainty estimates for these accuracies are unavailable.","Representations retain variation: item unit-normalized effective rank spans 28.23–47.18, while endpoint rank spans 15.30–30.83 across 200 identified training users per category. Identity and batch-reordering controls have zero difference in every category, but omitted calibration outcomes and unavailable real-fault evidence prevent broader correctness claims."],"key_implications":["The models consistently score training positives above sampled negatives, with Electronics showing the weakest observed separation.","Endpoint variation is more concentrated than item variation; neither effective rank nor angular alignment establishes useful ranking.","Available evidence supports stable sampled training behavior, while validation HR@10 and temporal relevance effects remain unestablished."],"evidence":{"headline_metrics":{"Movies_and_TV:pairwise_accuracy":0.9740105316799729,"Industrial_and_Scientific:pairwise_accuracy":0.9818824168855874,"Electronics:pairwise_accuracy":0.9292461924040871,"CDs_and_Vinyl:pairwise_accuracy":0.9965452056580405},"brief_metric_read":{"pairwise_accuracy":"Conditional on sampled negative difficulty; repeated training positions are not independent users.","representation_effective_rank":"Describes covariance concentration, not recommendation quality.","checks":"Identity and batch-order consistency pass; these controls alone do not establish correctness.","missing_evidence":"Validation interventions and candidate-depth audits are unavailable; detailed sensitivity and calibration results are omitted."}}}
